applies_why: No; the judge rests UNDERDETERMINED on the defender's recorded dropping of a limb, not on any single verse's failure to state a link or its contrary.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: Phrase: 'That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED.' Reading 1: it bars only a rationale explicitly grounded on single-verse insufficiency. Reading 2: it also bars a 'no live link remains to contradict' rationale when a verse is pressed against a dropped limb. I used Reading 1.
why: The judge's stated ground is the defender's recorded dropping of the curse limb, not that a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary, so K-S2 is obeyed.
